text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerians wept at airport over hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 enroute from Addis Ababa to Abidjan via Lagos which crashed into the sea near Comoros Islands.
- Union Bank, one of Nigeria's four biggest commercial banks, opens office in South Africa.
- Robbers steal 87 mail bags from state-run Nigerian Postal Service from delivery van.

- Nation's number two Lieutnant-General Oladipo Diya tells a rally in southwestern Ile-Ife to mark Ile-Ife Day that the military government's economic and political programmes were yielding positive results.
- Visiting American stockbrokers and investors say they plan to inject about $50 million into the Nigerian capital market within the next 12 months.
- Nigerian capital Abuja has recorded 100 deaths between last September till date due to the dreaded AIDS disease, Michael Momoh, coordinator of AIDS control programme in the inland capital, says.
- Nigerian government sends fact-finding team to Europe to ascertain actual balances left in foreign accounts owned by state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) and Central Bank.
- Rescue team to begin on Monday dredging work to facilitate recovery of fuselage of Nigerian airliner which crashed three weeks ago in a lagoon near Lagos, killing all 142 on board.
